mood.p: Vrijdag 4 september begint onstuimig: een regengebied trekt in de ochtend van noordwest naar zuidoost over het land, met vooral in het noorden flinke regen en een vrij krachtige tot harde zuidwestenwind van 5 tot 7 Bft en windstoten tot 80 kilometer per uur aan de kust. In de loop van de middag klaart het vanuit het noordwesten op, met maxima van zo'n 17 graden in het noorden tot lokaal 24 graden in Limburg, en het weekend belooft droger en warmer weer met zondag en maandag zomerse waarden tot 27 graden. De stemming in het land is grimmiger dan het weer: de aanval van tientallen gewapende mannen in Overasselt houdt de gemoederen bezig, de burgemeester sluit het pand van Jan G. een jaar en minister Van Weel spreekt van ongekend geweld. In Den Haag rommelt het rond de begroting nu het minderheidskabinet-Jetten de bezuinigingen op de sociale zekerheid grotendeels heeft geschrapt maar weigert de plannen voor Prinsjesdag openbaar te maken. Automobilisten voelen de Iranoorlog aan de pomp, met een nieuw record van 2,69 euro voor een liter Euro95, en woensdag 9 september ligt het hele openbaar vervoer een dag plat. Toch is er ook opluchting: het landelijke watertekort is officieel afgeschaald en de honderdste warme dag van het jaar is al geteld.

global.h3: Iran fires missiles and drones at US bases in Kuwait and UAE
global.summary: Tehran struck back on 3 September after the US resumed airstrikes on Iranian targets, sending missiles and suicide drones at Ahmed Al Jaber Air Base in Kuwait and Al Minhad in the UAE.
body: Iran's army said early on Thursday 3 September that it had launched ballistic missiles and one-way attack drones at American military positions in Kuwait and the United Arab Emirates. Iranian state media claimed hits on satellite communications systems, equipment warehouses and hangars housing US fighter jets at Kuwait's Ahmed Al Jaber Air Base, as well as radar installations at Al Minhad Air Base near Dubai.

Kuwait's army said its air defences intercepted the incoming barrage and described the attacks as heinous. It was the second day running that Kuwaiti batteries were engaged, and Gulf News reported that Bahrain and Jordan were also targeted. The salvo followed US strikes on Iranian missile and radar infrastructure on 1 and 2 September that Tehran says killed at least 18 people.

The exchange marks the sharpest escalation since the June ceasefire that was meant to calm the seven-month conflict. Analysts warned that renewed strikes around the Strait of Hormuz threaten the fragile recovery in tanker traffic, and Brent crude pushed back above 96 dollars a barrel on the news.

global.h3: Vance: 'I wouldn't call it a war' as US probes wedding strike
global.summary: Standing in at the White House podium, the vice president dismissed Iranian claims that a US strike hit a wedding party and described the latest exchanges as occasional flare-ups.
body: Vice President JD Vance told reporters on 3 September that he was extremely skeptical of Iranian reports that an American strike earlier in the week hit a home hosting a wedding. Iranian officials say four people died and close to 70 were wounded in that strike. Vance said the US was looking into the claim but had no information either way, adding that unlike the IRGC the United States does not target civilians.

Asked whether the conflict that began in February would be over before the November midterms, Vance replied that he would not call it a war right now, saying there was no active shooting and characterising the recent strikes from both sides as flare-ups. Vance has been handling press briefings since Karoline Leavitt left her role as press secretary at the end of August.

global.h3: Katz: Israel ready to remove Gaza's population if US agrees
global.summary: Israel's defence minister said the government is organised to move Palestinians out of Gaza by sea and air pending American approval, as Ben-Gvir presented a 20-page emigration plan.
body: Defence Minister Israel Katz told a news conference on Wednesday 2 September that Israel is prepared to remove Palestinians from the Gaza Strip by every means possible if Washington gives the green light. He argued there is no lasting solution for Gaza without what he called migration and said the main obstacle is finding countries willing to take people in.

National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir followed up with a document titled National Work Plan for Voluntary Emigration from the Gaza Strip, which he presented as a solution to the conflict. Prime Minister Netanyahu has said Israel controls about 60 percent of Gaza and will not withdraw until Hamas disarms.

global.h3: Israel snatches Hamas security chief; Hamas warns truce may collapse
global.summary: Shin Bet and IDF forces used a disguised vegetable truck in a daylight raid in Gaza City to seize Muein al-Arabid, prompting Hamas to warn the ceasefire could break down entirely.
body: Israeli special forces captured a man Israel identifies as Hamas's internal security chief in Gaza during a rare daytime operation in western Gaza City on Tuesday 1 September. Netanyahu praised the raid and accused al-Arabid of hiding hostages and rebuilding Hamas forces. Palestinian accounts say the detainee's wife was killed and that he is a lower-ranking officer.

Hamas responded that the raid showed Israel has no intention of honouring the truce and warned that the already shaky ceasefire could collapse completely. FDD's Long War Journal counted 29 reported ceasefire violations between 19 August and 3 September.

global.h3: More than 900 killed in Gaza this year despite ceasefire
global.summary: The Hamas-run health ministry says over 900 Palestinians have died since January, with conflict monitor ACLED documenting continued targeted strikes throughout the truce.
body: The BBC reported on 2 September that the health ministry in Gaza has recorded more than 900 deaths in 2026 even though a ceasefire has formally been in place since October 2025. ACLED, which tracks conflict incidents, said Israeli strikes during the truce have targeted Hamas operatives, including commanders linked to the 7 October 2023 attack.

Analysts quoted by the BBC said Gaza has effectively experienced a partial war under the label of a ceasefire, with Israel holding about 60 percent of the territory and expanding its zone of control. Aid agencies say access remains heavily restricted.

global.h3: Russian drones hit Coca-Cola plant near Kyiv, Zelensky calls it a signal to US
global.summary: Shahed-type drones damaged the American-owned bottling plant in Brovary on 3 September, with no injuries reported.
body: Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said in his evening address on Thursday that Russian drones struck a Coca-Cola production facility just east of Kyiv. Officials reported no casualties but significant damage to the site in Brovary. Zelensky said Moscow could not have been unaware that the plant is an American asset and called the strike a clear Russian signal to America.

The attack came a day after Russia deliberately targeted Ukraine's railway network, killing six Ukrzaliznytsia employees in Kyiv, and as the Washington Post reported that jet-powered Russian drones are increasingly overwhelming Ukrainian air defences.

global.h3: Putin floats 'chance' of peace as Rutte calls Russia increasingly reckless
global.summary: The Russian president said Moscow and Kyiv must settle the war between themselves, while NATO's chief pointed to drones over the eastern flank and the Leipzig sabotage attempt.
body: Speaking on 3 September, Vladimir Putin said there was a chance for peace with Ukraine but insisted the problem must be resolved by Russia and Ukraine alone. He again labelled Kyiv's warning to airlines about Russian airspace as state terrorism. Bloomberg reported that he offered little sign of progress on territory or security guarantees.

NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte replied that Russia is becoming increasingly reckless, citing missiles and drones crossing into allied airspace and the attempted drone attack on Leipzig airport last month. He said allies would not be divided or deterred from supporting Ukraine.

global.h3: Zelensky calls shootout between Kyiv's spy agencies 'shameful'
global.summary: A gunfight between the SBU security service and the GUR military intelligence agency in central Kyiv left several wounded and exposed a bitter turf war.
body: Personnel from Ukraine's SBU and its military intelligence counterpart GUR exchanged fire overnight in central Kyiv, in an incident reportedly linked to a dispute over the commander of a controversial unit. Zelensky condemned the clash as absolutely shameful and said Ukrainian weapons should only be pointed at Russian occupiers.
The Guardian's war briefing on 3 September said the president ordered an investigation and that three people were hurt. Russian state media seized on the episode as evidence of disorder in Kyiv.

global.h3: Germany blames Russia for Leipzig airport drone plot, EU vows response
global.summary: Berlin closed the Russian House and the Bonn consulate after linking an explosive-laden drone found near a Ukrainian plane to Russian hybrid operations.
body: Germany formally attributed the attempted drone attack at Leipzig/Halle airport to Russia on 1 September. Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said the incident, in which a drone carrying explosives was found near a Ukrainian aircraft on the night of 4 to 5 August, fits the known pattern of Russian hybrid operations in Europe.

Berlin ordered the Russian House in Berlin and the Russian consulate in Bonn to close, with staff given seven days to leave. German prosecutors are also investigating fresh sabotage cases, and Reuters reported on 2 September that the EU intends to hit back with new measures against Moscow.

global.h3: UN probe: foreign weapons and drones sustain Sudan's war
global.summary: A UN fact-finding mission says external networks supply both sides and that drone strikes killed more than 1,000 people in the first five months of 2026, some possibly war crimes.
body: The UN fact-finding mission on Sudan published a report on 3 September concluding that foreign weapons, military technology, fighters and logistics are prolonging the conflict and expanding both parties' ability to strike deep into civilian areas. It documented drone attacks on hospitals, schools, markets and displacement sites.

Investigators traced a transnational supply network involving the UAE, Chad, Libya and Somalia to the Rapid Support Forces, including roughly 2,000 Colombian contractors operating drones. The National reported the army has also used foreign-supplied drones, including a strike that killed at least 70 people at a teaching hospital in East Darfur.

global.h3: Brent tops $96 as Gulf attacks hit Hormuz reopening hopes
global.summary: Oil jumped after Iran's strikes on Kuwait, Iran's rial sank to a record low and Tehran listed 11 more ships as non-compliant with its rules for the strait.
body: Brent crude climbed above 96 dollars a barrel on 3 September, with some trading near 99 dollars in the US morning, after Iran fired at US bases in Kuwait and the UAE. Tanker transits through Hormuz had recovered to a wartime record of more than 17 million barrels on Monday under US naval protection, still short of the 20 million barrels a day seen before the war began on 28 February.

Iran's currency fell to a fresh low on 2 September, with the euro trading above 2.55 million rials, after the UAE cut financial ties and Washington launched what it calls Operation Economic Exclusion. Reuters reported that Tehran declared another 11 vessels non-compliant and liable to fines or seizure.

global.h3: Chevron pledges $7bn to double Venezuelan oil output
global.summary: The US major will develop two Orinoco Belt fields over five years as Energy Secretary Chris Wright touted tens of billions in deals during a visit to Caracas.
body: Chevron announced on 2 September that it will invest more than 7 billion dollars in its Venezuelan joint ventures over the next five years, aiming to lift output to about 600,000 barrels a day. The company gains the Carabobo 1 and Carabobo-2-South-A blocks next to its existing Petroindependencia venture with state firm PDVSA.

US Energy Secretary Chris Wright, speaking in Venezuela, said the oil and gas agreements are vital to transforming the country and creating jobs. The deal follows a US government stake in a Venezuelan oil venture announced days earlier.

global.h3: Canada's counter-tariffs on 700 US goods take effect 8 September
global.summary: Ottawa's retaliation for Washington's 50 percent tariffs targets steel, dairy, appliances and electronics as Trump brands Canada one of the worst trade abusers.
body: US tariffs of 50 percent on roughly 27.6 billion dollars of Canadian goods took effect on 22 August, covering dairy, alcohol, building materials, apparel and agricultural products. Canada announced its response on 25 August: counter-tariffs on more than 700 items that start on 8 September.

President Trump has called Canada one of the worst abusers in trade and said he does not want US businesses importing Canadian goods. Al Jazeera's analysis says the tit-for-tat measures hit products previously shielded by the USMCA, putting the pact's future in doubt.

global.h3: Burnham survives first PMQs as Starmer quits Parliament
global.summary: The new UK prime minister promised to bring back hope and fully fund defence, while his predecessor announced he will leave the Commons after 11 years.
body: Andy Burnham faced his first Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday 2 September, six weeks after winning the Labour leadership. He announced a VAT cut on electricity bills, lower business rates for pubs and music venues and a two-pound bus fare cap for 2027, and pledged a ten-year plan before the end of the year.

Bloomberg said the debut offered more style than specifics, and Labour backbencher Tan Dhesi warned that vibes alone will not be enough on defence. Burnham said the government will fully fund the Defence Investment Plan and meet NATO commitments by 2035.

global.h3: AfD eyes first state government in Sunday's Saxony-Anhalt vote
global.summary: Polls put the far-right party above 40 percent ahead of the 6 September election, with an outright majority possible if smaller parties miss the 5 percent threshold.
body: Voters in Saxony-Anhalt go to the polls on Sunday 6 September in the first of three eastern German state elections this month. An INSA survey puts the AfD at 42 to 43 percent, with Chancellor Friedrich Merz's CDU at 22 percent.

The AfD could win a majority of seats if the SPD, Greens, FDP and BSW all fall below 5 percent, which would produce the first AfD-led state government in German history. All centrist parties say they will maintain the firewall against coalition with the party, and almost a third of voters remain undecided.

global.h3: Guinea-Bissau approves constitution that expands presidential power
global.summary: Provisional results show 70 percent backed the junta-backed charter, which lets the president sack the cabinet and dissolve parliament ahead of December elections.
body: Guinea-Bissau's electoral commission announced on 1 September that 70 percent of voters approved a new constitution in Sunday's referendum, on turnout of nearly 60 percent. The military leaders who seized power after the disputed November 2025 vote say the changes will end chronic instability.

Under the new text the president can appoint and dismiss the prime minister and ministers, create or abolish ministries and dissolve parliament in a serious crisis. Parliament shrinks and new rules govern who can stand as a candidate.

global.h3: Joshua Wong pleads guilty to foreign collusion charge
global.summary: The jailed Hong Kong activist admitted a second national security offence that carries up to life in prison, likely extending his time behind bars.
body: Joshua Wong, 29, answered guilty at Hong Kong's High Court on Wednesday 2 September to a charge of conspiring to collude with foreign forces. Prosecutors say he worked with exiled activist Nathan Law and others in 2020 to seek sanctions and other hostile measures against the Hong Kong and Chinese governments.
Wong is already serving four years and eight months for subversion in the landmark 47 democrats case and had been expected to be released as early as 2027. Sentencing on the new charge will follow.

global.h3: Trump asks Supreme Court to unblock USPS mail-ballot restrictions
global.summary: The Justice Department filed an emergency request on 3 September to lift Judge Talwani's order that stops the Postal Service implementing the president's mail-voting order before the midterms.
body: The Trump administration asked the Supreme Court on Thursday to intervene after Judge Indira Talwani refused to lift her block on new US Postal Service rules for handling mail ballots. Talwani accused the government of a cynical reading of an earlier Supreme Court ruling that had sided with Trump on the executive order itself.
A whistleblower has alleged that USPS repeatedly defied court orders to advance the plan. Talwani is due to hold a hearing on a longer-lasting preliminary injunction.

global.h3: Cholera spreads to West Kordofan as airstrike destroys WFP food convoy
global.summary: WHO flagged Sudan's West Kordofan as the latest cholera hotspot with 10 deaths, while the World Food Programme condemned an aerial attack on aid trucks bound for South Kordofan.
body: At least 10 people have died and more than 40 have been infected in a new cholera outbreak in West Kordofan, according to a WHO update reported by Dabanga on 3 September. Humanitarian agencies say they are stepping up vaccination and treatment amid fighting and shrinking funds.

The World Food Programme said an aerial attack destroyed trucks carrying a large food shipment for hungry families in South Kordofan, calling attacks on humanitarian operations unacceptable. Dabanga also reported about 6,200 malnourished children in Malha, North Darfur.

global.h3: Edouard dumps over 20 inches of rain on Texas and Louisiana
global.summary: The tropical storm made landfall at Johnson Bayou on 1 September, knocked out power to 150,000 customers and triggered a rare high flood risk as it weakened inland.
body: Tropical Storm Edouard came ashore near Johnson Bayou, Louisiana, on Tuesday afternoon with 60 mph winds, barely a day after forming in the Gulf. It downed trees and power lines, leaving more than 150,000 customers without electricity across southwest Louisiana and the upper Texas coast.

By Wednesday 2 September Edouard had weakened to a tropical depression but continued to pour rain over southeast Texas, where the National Weather Service issued a high risk of excessive rainfall for the Big Thicket and Piney Woods. CNN reported rescues and totals above 20 inches in places.

global.h3: Haiti: 5.8 million face acute hunger as drought threat grows
global.summary: France 24 reporting from the ground describes gang violence, 1.4 million displaced and a looming dry spell in what Guterres calls the hemisphere's worst crisis.
body: A France 24 report published on 2 September paints Haiti as living through one of the worst humanitarian crises in its recent history, with 5.8 million people facing acute food insecurity and more than 1.4 million displaced by armed gang violence.

UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres, who visited Port-au-Prince in June, has described Haiti as facing the most severe crisis in the Western Hemisphere and the third worst in the world after Palestine and Sudan, with 6.4 million people in need of assistance.

netherlands.h3: Overasselt: home of Jan G. shut for a year after armed raid
netherlands.summary: The mayor of Heumen closed the farmhouse for twelve months and barred its occupant from the municipality for two weeks, as police found more weapons and a threat video circulated.
body: Mayor Joerie Minsens announced on Thursday 3 September that the property on the Ewijkseweg in Overasselt will be closed for a year and that Jan G. may not enter the municipality for two weeks. Cameras will be installed around the site to restore calm in the village of 2,800 people, where residents told NOS they hope G. leaves for good.

The measures follow Tuesday's attack in which dozens of masked men, some with heavy firearms, marched through the village and shot dead a security guard at the farm. Two police officers were injured and 34 people were arrested. Police later found several pistols in searches around the village and are investigating a video in which armed men threaten G. over a missing 1,283 kilo cocaine shipment.

Justice Minister David van Weel called the violence unprecedented and new for the Netherlands, while NRC noted that heavy drug violence is not new but that shifting cocaine supply routes have brought it to rural areas.

netherlands.h3: Cabinet refuses to publish leaked budget despite Kamer majority
netherlands.summary: Finance Minister Heinen told MPs the minority cabinet will wait for Prinsjesdag, a day after details showed most social security cuts scrapped and 1.5 billion euro for purchasing power.
body: A majority in the Tweede Kamer asked the Jetten cabinet on 2 September to publish the financial plans that D66, VVD and CDA agreed after weeks of wrangling, but Finance Minister Eelco Heinen wrote that the government will not release them before Prinsjesdag on 15 September.

The leaked Prinsjesdag papers show the 2.8 billion euro cut to the AOW is off, the faster rise in the pension age is dropped, the 20 percent reduction in the maximum daily wage is scrapped and the halving of the WW duration is delayed a year. To win opposition support, 1.5 billion euro goes to purchasing power and taxes on high incomes rise by 750 million.

netherlands.h3: Box 3 wealth tax reform postponed again, now to 2029
netherlands.summary: The coalition failed to find a political fix for the actual-return tax law that stalled in the Senate, and the tax office says its IT cannot handle new policy before 2028.
body: Plans to tax actual returns on savings and investments are set to be delayed by another year, DutchNews reported on 2 September, meaning the Wet Werkelijk Rendement is unlikely to take effect before 2029. The bill ran aground in the Eerste Kamer just before the summer and the coalition partners could not agree a way through.
NRC reported that the Belastingdienst's slow IT modernisation leaves the cabinet with its hands tied, with State Secretary Eelco Eerenberg saying room for new policy wishes only returns from 2028.

netherlands.h3: Media watchdog clears minister to pull Ongehoord Nederland's licence
netherlands.summary: The Commissariaat voor de Media handed Rianne Letschert the facts she needs to remove the far-right broadcaster from the public system after a Hitler segment.
body: The Commissariaat voor de Media said on 3 September that Media Minister Rianne Letschert (D66) may revoke the broadcasting licence of Ongehoord Nederland. The regulator supplied what it called facts and considerations supporting removal, describing a recent fragment glorifying Hitler as a tipping point.

ON has been repeatedly fined and warned since joining the public system, and the latest controversy erupted in recent weeks. The minister must now decide whether to act, a step no government has taken against a public broadcaster before.

netherlands.h3: Cabinet wants to detain more asylum seekers for Dublin transfers
netherlands.summary: A pilot by the asylum ministry aims to hold applicants so they can be handed over to the EU country responsible for their claim.
body: NRC reported on 3 September that the Ministry of Asylum and Migration is starting a trial to detain asylum seekers more often so they can actually be transferred to the European country where they first applied. Many Dublin transfers currently fail because people disappear before the handover.
The plan fits the Jetten cabinet's push to cut inflow while staying within EU rules, and it comes weeks before the new EU migration pact starts to apply.

netherlands.h3: Netherlands pushes to keep UN peacekeepers in Lebanon past December
netherlands.summary: Foreign Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma told The National he is pressing Israel to withdraw from south Lebanon and wants UNIFIL's mandate extended beyond the 31 December deadline.
body: Dutch Foreign Minister Sjoerd Sjoerdsma said in an interview published on 3 September that the Netherlands supports extending the UNIFIL mission in Lebanon beyond its scheduled end on 31 December, calling it important for the country's stability.
He said The Hague is applying pressure on Israel to pull its forces out of southern Lebanon, where they have remained since the 2024 war with Hezbollah.

netherlands.h3: DNB moves 86 tonnes of gold out of US and Canada to London
netherlands.summary: The central bank cited rising geopolitical unrest and said reserves can be sold faster in a crisis from the Bank of England's vaults.
body: De Nederlandsche Bank announced on Wednesday 2 September that it relocated about 86 tonnes of gold, worth roughly 10 billion dollars, from New York and Ottawa between March and August. That is more than a quarter of the 313 tonnes it held in North America.

Part of the transfer was done by buying and selling, and 27 tonnes were physically flown to the Netherlands while an equivalent amount meeting Bank of England standards moved from the Zeist vault to London. DNB framed the move as crisis preparedness because gold can be sold quickly in London.

netherlands.h3: Petrol hits new record of 2.69 euro a litre and keeps climbing
netherlands.summary: The advisory price for Euro95 reached 2.692 euro on 3 September after breaking the May record a day earlier, driven by the Iran war and Hormuz disruption.
body: The recommended price for a litre of Euro95 rose to 2.692 euro on Thursday, a day after passing the previous record of 2.646 euro set on 6 May. Diesel is also near its peak.

NOS reported that despite the record, motorists keep driving, while UnitedConsumers' Paul van Selms told Hart van Nederland there is little prospect of cheaper fuel soon. Prices have surged since the outbreak of the Iran war in late February because a fifth of global oil normally passes through the Strait of Hormuz.

netherlands.h3: Nationwide 24-hour public transport strike goes ahead on 9 September
netherlands.summary: FNV's rail, regional and city transport members will down tools next Wednesday over the social security cuts, halting NS, ProRail, buses, trams and metros.
body: FNV Spoor, FNV Streekvervoer and FNV Stadsvervoer are calling on staff across the sector to stop work for 24 hours on Wednesday 9 September. Regional transport stops from the start of service, and exact times for NS and city transport are being announced this week.

The unions say the partial retreat by the cabinet on benefit cuts does not meet their ultimatum, which demanded all social security cuts be withdrawn. Universities, courts and the Raad van State are telling people to plan for a day without trains and buses.

netherlands.h3: Student housing shortage barely shrinks despite new builds
netherlands.summary: The national monitor puts the gap at 20,200 rooms against 21,000 last year, even though construction targets are being met.
body: The Landelijke Monitor Studentenhuisvesting published on 3 September estimates the shortage of student rooms at just over 20,200, down only slightly from 21,000 in 2025. Cities and universities are delivering the new homes they promised, but demand keeps pace.
Rotterdam, Amsterdam and Utrecht remain the tightest markets as international student numbers stabilise and domestic students stay at home longer.

netherlands.h3: Freelancers have 42 percent less work than two years ago
netherlands.summary: Assignments for zzp'ers have collapsed since late 2024 as clients react to stricter enforcement of bogus self-employment rules.
body: NL Times reported on 3 September that the number of assignments available to freelancers is 42 percent lower than at the end of 2024. Intermediaries attribute the drop to companies avoiding zzp contracts since the tax office resumed enforcement of the DBA law in January 2025.
Many former freelancers have moved into salaried jobs or agency work, while others in IT, healthcare and construction report long gaps between contracts.

netherlands.h3: National water shortage downgraded, but effects will linger for months
netherlands.summary: The infrastructure ministry scaled the status back from official shortage to threatening shortage after recent rain, warning that groundwater and nature need far longer to recover.
body: The Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management decided on 3 September to downgrade the national water situation from an official water shortage to a threatening water shortage. Rain in recent weeks lifted river levels and eased pressure on drinking water supplies.
Officials cautioned that the summer drought's impact on groundwater, agriculture and nature will be felt for months or even years, and some regional restrictions on irrigation stay in place.

netherlands.h3: West Nile virus confirmed in nine people this summer
netherlands.summary: Health authorities say the mosquito-borne infection is now established in the Netherlands after a warm season.
body: Nine people in the Netherlands have been diagnosed with West Nile virus since the start of the summer, NL Times reported on 3 September. Most had mild symptoms, but the virus can cause serious neurological illness in older or vulnerable patients.
The RIVM has been monitoring birds and mosquitoes since the first domestic cases in 2020, and the warm summer of 2026 created favourable conditions for the Culex mosquitoes that spread it.

netherlands.h3: Dutch swimming water still polluted, with flea-collar pesticide widespread
netherlands.summary: Research by an environmental group and the NIOO found chemicals and bacteria at many official swim sites, and chemical pollution has worsened.
body: A study by an environmental organisation and the Netherlands Institute of Ecology, reported on 3 September, found that swimming water at official sites is still frequently contaminated with bacteria and chemicals. The pesticide used in dog flea collars turned up at many locations.
Researchers said chemical pollution has grown worse compared with earlier surveys, even where bacterial quality meets EU standards.

netherlands.h3: 2.5 million Dutch victims of cybercrime as threats change rapidly
netherlands.summary: Police and the NCSC warned that scams and hacks are evolving fast, with AI-driven fraud among the fastest growing categories.
body: Dutch authorities said on 3 September that an estimated 2.5 million people fell victim to cybercrime or online fraud last year. They described the threat landscape as changing rapidly, with criminals adopting AI tools for phishing and voice cloning.
Bank helpdesk fraud, WhatsApp scams and investment fraud remain the most common forms, and only a fraction of victims file police reports.
